post.description: Creates the person, their first Project and its API key in one call, and signs them in. This is US0: the API key exists at the moment of registration and not after it. The key is shown here and nowhere else — only its prefix and a hash are stored, so no endpoint can return it again.

201.description: The person, their Project, the API key in full, and a live session.

409.description: `email_taken`. The address already has an account — sign in instead.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. The email must be one, and the password between 12 and 128 characters.

post.summary: Register, and receive a Project and an API key

post.description: Exchanges an email and a password for a session token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` from then on. Send `device` and a Device is created holding that session: that is what the app does, and what makes it able to answer a Request. Omit it and no Device is written, which is what the dashboard does — a browser session may read nothing an installation reads.

200.description: A live session, and the id of the Device that was born with it when one was asked for.

401.description: `invalid_credentials`. One answer for a wrong password and for an address with no account alike — telling them apart would make this endpoint a way of asking who has an account.

post.summary: Sign in, and — if this is the app — bring a Device into existence

post.description: Deletes the session behind the bearer token, which also detaches it from the Device that was holding it. Always answers `204`, including for a token that was already dead: signing out is a state to arrive at, not an operation to succeed at, and a 401 here would tell an unauthenticated caller which tokens are live.

204.description: The session is gone, or never was.

post.description: Always answers `204`, whether or not the address has an account, and takes about as long either way. The email carries a link into the dashboard holding a token that lives for one hour.

204.description: Taken. Nothing here says whether anything was sent.

post.description: The token is the one in the emailed link, and it can be spent once. Existing sessions are not ended by this — device revocation is stage 3, and #33 says so rather than half-implementing it here.

204.description: The password is the new one.

400.description: `invalid_reset_token`. Spent, expired, or never issued. Ask for another.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. The password must be between 12 and 128 characters.

post.summary: Spend a reset token and set a new password

post.description: Creates a pending Request and validates its Surface against the catalog. Send `Idempotency-Key` only if you retry automatically: the returned `requestId` is already the identity of the Request. Send `callbackUrl` to be called once, with a signed `POST`, when the Request reaches a terminal state — that is what an n8n "Ask & wait" node resumes on, and the alternative to holding a long poll open.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Send only if you retry automatically. The same key with the same request returns the Request already created, with `200`; with a different request it is a `422`.

200.description: This `Idempotency-Key` had already created this exact Request. Nothing was created; the original Request is returned as it stands now.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

422.description: `surface_invalid` names the component and property at fault, the `root` the renderer would not find, or the quick action whose `name` is not an action the surface dispatches; `idempotency_conflict` means this key was already used for a different request; `callback_url_invalid` means the `callbackUrl` is not a public `https` endpoint this API is willing to call; `invalid_request_body` is a malformed envelope.

get.description: Returns the Request as it stands now, without waiting. The same body as `GET /v1/requests/{id}/response`: read `status` to tell a Response from an outcome without one, and `status: "pending"` — nobody has answered yet — from `expired`, where the Request timed out. `deliveredAt` and `readAt` are the two receipts: a `pending` Request with both null never reached a phone, which is a different problem from one nobody has answered. Use the long poll instead when you intend to wait for the answer.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `requestId` returned when the Request was created.

200.description: The Request as it stands. `response` is present exactly when `status` is `answered`.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

404.description: `request_not_found`. A Request belonging to another Project answers the same way as one that does not exist.

delete.description: Moves a pending Request to `cancelled`: the agent no longer needs the answer. Nothing is deleted — the Request stays readable, and `cancelled` is what tells the agent later that it withdrew rather than the person letting it lapse. A Request that reached any terminal state first is a `409` naming that state; `request_already_answered` means the person won the race and there is a Response to read.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `requestId` returned when the Request was created.

200.description: The Request was withdrawn. `response` is always null here.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

404.description: `request_not_found`. A Request belonging to another Project answers the same way as one that does not exist.

409.description: The Request was already terminal — the code names which state won: `request_already_answered`, `request_already_expired`, `request_already_dismissed` or `request_already_cancelled`.

post.description: Fires the push for a Request that is still waiting, without creating a second Request and without touching its state — no `status`, no `sequence`, no timestamp changes. Distinct from withdrawing and re-sending, which produces a `cancelled` Request and a new one. It obeys the priority the Request was created with and the recipient's quiet hours exactly as the first push did, so a `normal` Request nudged at three in the morning does not ring. A Request that already reached a terminal state is a `409` naming that state, never a silent no-op.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `requestId` returned when the Request was created.

200.description: The push was queued again. The Request is unchanged, and is returned as it stands.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

404.description: `request_not_found`. A Request belonging to another Project answers the same way as one that does not exist.

409.description: The Request is no longer pending, so there is nothing to re-notify — the code names which state it reached: `request_already_answered`, `request_already_expired`, `request_already_dismissed` or `request_already_cancelled`.

get.description: Resolves as soon as the Request reaches a terminal state, or when `wait` seconds have passed. Always a `200`: read `status` to tell a Response from an outcome without one, and `status: "pending"` — the Wait window ran out, the Request is still waiting — from `expired`, where the Request itself timed out. Re-issue on `pending`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `requestId` returned when the Request was created.

200.description: What awaiting the Request resolved to. `response` is present exactly when `status` is `answered`.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

404.description: `request_not_found`. A Request belonging to another Project answers the same way as one that does not exist.

422.description: `invalid_request_body` — `wait` must be a whole number of seconds between 0 and 30.

get.summary: Await the outcome of a Request

post.description: Records the A2UI action the person chose and moves the Request to `answered`, both in one transaction. The `context` is stored and republished to the agent exactly as sent; it is never inspected (ADR-0003).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `requestId` the notification carried.

200.description: The Request as it now stands, with the Response that closed it.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `request_not_found`. A Request belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

409.description: The Request was already terminal — the code names which state won: `request_already_answered`, `request_already_expired`, `request_already_dismissed` or `request_already_cancelled`.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `timestamp` must be RFC3339 in UTC (`2026-08-10T12:00:00Z`); `surfaceId`, if sent, must be this Request.

post.description: Moves the Request to `dismissed` without creating a Response. Distinct from letting it expire: the agent learns that the person actively declined.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `requestId` the notification carried.

200.description: The Request as it now stands. `response` is always null here.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `request_not_found`. A Request belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

409.description: The Request was already terminal — the code names which state won.

get.description: Both halves in one list, oldest first — `environment` says which is which. The signing secret is not here and is not on these rows: one Project has one secret, and `GET /v1/projects` returns it. An endpoint that is `disabled` is not a destination at all: no delivery is attempted and none is queued.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project whose endpoints these are.

200.description: The endpoints. An empty list is the ordinary answer for a Project nobody has configured.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

get.summary: The standing subscriptions of a Project

post.description: The other half of the webhooks, and it does not replace the per-Request `callbackUrl` — ADR-0014 decided the two stand beside each other. A Request that carries a `callbackUrl` **and** matches a subscription here produces two deliveries of the same event, to the two addresses; delivery is at-least-once by PRD §4.1 and both carry the same `id` and the same `responseId`, so a receiver behind both deduplicates them exactly as it deduplicates a retry. Every delivery is signed with the Project’s `webhookSigningSecret` — the same one that signs a per-Request callback, because there is only one. The URL is checked before the row exists: `https` only, no credentials in the userinfo, and every address the hostname resolves to must be public.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project this endpoint belongs to.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

409.description: `webhook_endpoint_duplicate`. This half of the Project already subscribes that URL — a second row would deliver every event to it twice, for nothing.

422.description: `invalid_request_body` for a malformed body, `webhook_url_invalid` for a URL this server may not dial.

patch.description: `status: "disabled"` is how an endpoint is silenced without being forgotten — nothing is enqueued for it, so there is nothing to retry and nothing to dead-letter. `environment` is not editable: moving a subscription between the halves of a Project is a different subscription, not an edited address, and doing it in one step is how live events end up at a rehearsal endpoint.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project the endpoint belongs to.

parameters.name: endpointId
parameters.description: The `id` of the endpoint.

200.description: The endpoint as it now stands.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

patch.summary: Change where an endpoint points, what it hears, or whether it hears

delete.description: The row is deleted rather than revoked, unlike an ApiKey: nothing points at an endpoint, so nothing loses its provenance. Deliveries already queued still go out — the job carries the URL it was created with — so a duplicate arriving just after a delete is the same at-least-once a receiver already deduplicates.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project the endpoint belongs to.

parameters.name: endpointId
parameters.description: The `id` of the endpoint.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

404.description: `webhook_endpoint_not_found`. Not this Project’s endpoint, or not an endpoint at all.

put.description: Records the push token, the platform and the catalog version compiled into this build (ADR-0002), and marks the Device as seen. Idempotent: the app calls it at every launch and after every token rotation. A push token already held by another Device is reassigned to this one — the operating systems recycle tokens across installations, and two rows holding the same token would mean every notification sent twice.

200.description: The Device as it now stands. The push token is not echoed back: it only ever travels towards the server.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `platform` must be `ios` or `android`, and `catalogVersion` a non-negative integer. A catalog version older than a surface needs is never an error here — it produces a warning on `POST /v1/requests` instead (ADR-0002).

get.description: Every Project the caller owns, newest first: pending Requests and unread notifications. Metadata only — the title and body come from the notification block, never from inside the Surface (ADR-0003). A Request whose expiry has just passed is still listed as `pending` until the sweep reaches it, at most a minute later; `expiresAt` is published so the app can say so. `environment` narrows the list to one half of the Projects — a rehearsal does ring, so leaving it off is how a person sees everything that was sent to them.

200.description: One page, newest first, and the cursor for the next one.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `limit` must be between 1 and 100; `cursor` must be a `nextCursor` this endpoint returned; `environment` must be `test` or `live`.

get.summary: List what is waiting for the person

get.description: The other half of the same list: Requests that reached a terminal state, and notifications that were read. Same page shape as the Inbox — every Message is in exactly one of the two, and `environment` narrows either of them the same way.

200.description: One page, newest first, and the cursor for the next one.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `limit` must be between 1 and 100; `cursor` must be a `nextCursor` this endpoint returned; `environment` must be `test` or `live`.

get.summary: List what no longer asks anything

get.description: The same row the list publishes, plus the Surface behind it — the one place this API hands Content back, and it hands it to the person it was written for. `surface` is null exactly when `minCatalogVersion` is: there is nothing rich to draw, and the notification block is the whole Message. The Surface goes out exactly as the agent sent it; the server neither renders nor inspects it (ADR-0003). Works for a Message in either list.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `messageId` of the row being opened.

200.description: The Message, with its Surface when it has one.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `message_not_found`. A Message belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

post.description: The Device confirming the push reached this phone, which is the only thing that actually knows: FCM confirms it *queued* a notification, not that it landed. Idempotent, and the first Device wins — a Message fans out to every Device of the recipient (PRD §4.3), and the receipt means *first confirmed*, not *all confirmed*. Called from the background handler when a push wakes a dead app, so it is expected to run without anything being opened. It never changes a `status`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `messageId` the push announced.

200.description: The row as it now stands, carrying the `deliveredAt` that was just stamped.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `message_not_found`. A Message belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

post.description: Records that the person saw it. Idempotent: the first read wins and a repeat returns the same `readAt`. Stamps `deliveredAt` too when nothing had — a Message can only be read on a phone it reached — so an `informational` Message travels `delivered → read` even when the push never arrived and the person found it in the list (PRD §4.2). For such a Message this is what moves it to the History: it has no `pending` and no expiry, so being read is how it finishes. It never changes a `status`: a Request is still answered or dismissed through `POST /v1/requests/{id}/response` or `/dismiss`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `messageId` of the row on screen.

200.description: The row as it now stands, ready to replace the one on screen.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `message_not_found`. A Message belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

get.description: The one read the dashboard makes. Keys are listed newest first and revoked ones are listed too, because a rotation is only legible if the key that was retired is still visible. No key is ever returned in full here: only its prefix exists to be read.

200.description: The Projects, oldest first. Registration leaves exactly one.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

get.summary: Every Project this person owns, with its API keys

patch.description: The only editable thing about a Project. Registration calls it `Default`, because US0 hands out a Project so that a key has somewhere to belong — this is where a person names it once they know what it is for.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The `projectId` registration returned.

200.description: The Project as it now stands, keys included.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

404.description: `project_not_found`. The same answer for a Project that is somebody else’s and for one that never existed — telling them apart would make this endpoint a way of asking which ids are real.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. The name must be between 1 and 80 characters.

post.description: The second and last place a whole credential exists in a readable form — the first is registration. Only its prefix and a SHA-256 are stored, so nothing can return it again. `environment` says which half of the Project the key speaks for and is required: the prefix it comes back with — `sk_test_…` or `sk_live_…` — is what an SDK reads its own environment from, and a key of one half neither creates nor reads the Requests of the other. Minting does not revoke anything: rotating is mint, put the new key in the agent, then revoke the old one, in that order, so that nothing stops working in between.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project the key will speak for.

201.description: The new key, in full. Copy it now.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

post.summary: Mint an API key, and read it once

delete.description: From the next request onwards the key answers `401 api_key_revoked`, which is its own code precisely so the developer is told to swap the credential rather than hunt a typo. The row is never deleted: the Messages it sent point at it, and that is what answers "what did this key send" without an audit log. Repeatable — revoking a revoked key changes nothing and keeps the original date.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The Project the key belongs to.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description: The `id` of the key, as listed by `GET /v1/projects`.

204.description: The key is revoked, or already was.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_revoked`.

404.description: `api_key_not_found`. Not this Project’s key, or not a key at all.

get.description: The time zone and the quiet hours of the person signed in — the settings that decide whether a push is allowed to make a noise (PRD §4.5). They belong to the User, so they hold across every Project they own, and they survive a reinstall: the phone reads them back from here rather than remembering them locally.

200.description: The preferences as they stand. `quietHours` is null when none are set, which is where every account starts.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

put.description: Replaces them whole: what you send is what the person will have. `quietHours: null` clears the window, and clears `allowHigh` with it — there is no switch remembered behind a window that no longer exists. `PUT` because the app sends this every time the screen is saved, and twice in a row means the same thing as once.

200.description: The preferences as they now stand, read back from the row that was written.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `timezone` must be an IANA name the server knows, `start` and `end` must be `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock and must differ, and quiet hours cannot be set without a timezone to read them in.

get.description: Every conversation this key can see, the one that last spoke first. Metadata only: `lastMessage` is the notification block of the newest Message, never anything read out of a surface (ADR-0003). One-shot Requests are Threads of one and are listed too — their `threadKey` is null. The list is scoped to the half of the Project the key belongs to: a `sk_test_…` never sees a live conversation.

200.description: One page, newest activity first, and the cursor for the next one.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `limit` must be between 1 and 100; `cursor` must be a `nextCursor` this endpoint returned.

get.summary: List the Threads of this Project

get.description: The conversation the agent named, and its history in order — oldest first, mixed: the notification of a plain Request and the metadata of an interactive card read the same way, told apart by `interactionType`. Page forward with `after`, which is the `sequence` of the last Message you hold; `nextAfter` is null when the page reached the end. A one-shot Thread has no key and is not reachable here — read its Request with `GET /v1/requests/{id}`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The `threadKey` sent with the Requests of this conversation. URL-encode it: it is the agent’s own string and this API never parses it.

200.description: The Thread and one page of its Messages.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable key, `api_key_revoked` for a revoked one.

404.description: `thread_not_found`. A Thread of another Project — or of the other half of this one — answers the same way as a key nobody has used.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `after` must be a whole number; `limit` 1 to 100.

get.summary: Read one Thread by its key

get.description: The conversation as the person sees it: oldest first, with the Surface of every Message that has one, so a mixed history of text and interactive cards can be drawn in one call. `after` is the `sequence` of the last Message on screen — 0, or omitted, reads from the beginning. With `wait` the call holds until something arrives **in this Thread**: a notification, or a Message of any other conversation, never resolves it. Always a `200`; an empty `items` means the window closed with nothing new, and the app re-issues from the same `after`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The `threadId` carried by every row of the Inbox and of the History.

200.description: The Messages after `after`, oldest first — empty if none arrived.

401.description: `unauthorized` for a missing or unusable session token, `session_revoked` for a device that was signed out.

404.description: `thread_not_found`. A Thread belonging to another person answers the same way as one that does not exist.

422.description: `invalid_request_body`. `after` must be a whole number; `limit` 1 to 100; `wait` a whole number of seconds between 0 and 30.

get.summary: Read a Thread, and wait for its next Message

post.description: Records an email and the two answers the waitlist form asks for. Unauthenticated, and accepted only from the Nibify site. Submitting the same email again is not an error: the answers are updated.

200.description: The Lead was recorded. The same answer whether the email was new or already on the list.

403.description: `origin_not_allowed` for a submission that did not come from the site; `submission_rejected` for one that looks automated.

422.description: `invalid_request_body` — a malformed email, or an answer outside its enumeration.

get.description: Fails if the process cannot reach Postgres, which is the only datastore (ADR-0004).

200.description: The process is up and Postgres answers.

info.title: Nibify API
info.description: The channel on which AI agents push interactive UI to a person and receive an answer back. This document is the source of truth every client is generated from.
